title: Kidney function tests (creatinine, urea, eGFR)
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It shows how well your kidneys clean your blood. eGFR is calculated from creatinine, age, and sex.
why: For high blood pressure, diabetes, swelling, before some scans with contrast dye, while taking certain medicines, or at a checkup.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come the next day
tell_doctor: What medicines you take, especially water pills and painkillers
If you take sports supplements, such as creatine
If you have a scan with contrast dye planned
If your results were abnormal before. Bring your past results

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually fasting: no food for 8 to 12 hours. Plain water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: No alcohol and no hard workouts. Do not eat a lot of meat in the evening.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything should change.

bring: Past test results, if you have them
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
Results usually come in 1 day. The lab will tell you when
Sometimes the doctor adds a urine test to get the full picture

faq.a: It is an estimate of how much blood your kidneys clean each minute. It is based on creatinine, age, and sex.

faq.q: Why can creatinine be high without illness?
faq.a: It depends on muscle mass, meat in your diet, exercise, and how much water you drink. So your doctor draws the conclusions.

reminders.text: Kidney tests tomorrow. Do not eat after dinner. Plain water is fine.
